subject: Observability combo — pricing & nonlinear credit structuring

Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Observability combo — initial pricing and credit options

Hi Samir,

Thanks again for your time today. Per our conversation I'm attaching a compact pricing matrix and a short note on how nonlinear credits can help OptiScale absorb high ingest spikes without a large committed slab. High-level proposal:

- Base observability add-on (retention + basic tracing): $0.18/GB-month retained after discounts
- Advanced dashboards (seat-based + query credits): $1,200 per seat / month with a 10-seat minimum
- Nonlinear credit tiers: discounts increase at 10TB, 50TB, and 200TB retained per month (see attachment)

Two things you asked to clarify: run-rate smoothing for seasonal spikes, and whether we can offer an initial concession tied to a 12-month commitment. Short answer: yes, we can propose a time-limited credit uplift for the first 6 months and taper thereafter.

Attachments: obs-pricing-matrix-v2.xlsx (matrix + examples), retention-tier-breakdown.pdf (tier math and examples).

Next steps: can you confirm the retention percentile (90th or 95th) you want us to use for the tier boundary calculations, and whether procurement needs a PO or a signed SOW first? I can draft a commercial term sheet to match.

Best,
Naomi Feldman

Naomi,

Appreciate the quick follow-up and attachments. A few clarifications from our side before we loop procurement:

1) For nonlinear credits — we need an example of how this performs on real traffic. Our monthly retention footprint is spiky: baseline ~18TB, occasional peaks to ~120TB during end-of-quarter pipelines. The 95th percentile would mask those peaks for us. Can you show an example using 95th retention?
2) Dashboard seats — we prefer unlimited viewers but locked editor seats. Can we map query credits to editor seats instead of a hard seat minimum?
3) Concession structure — a 6-month uplift is fine but procurement will want to see the net present value over 12 months and a clear step-down schedule.

Also, two non-negotiables from procurement: (a) a clause that caps overage exposure to 150% of committed tier in a single month, and (b) a one-time onboarding credit if we hit your recommended instrumentation milestones.

If you can supply the 95th-percentile example and a revised pricing sheet with the step-down, I can get procurement eyes on it this week.

Thanks,
Samir
VP of Engineering | OptiScale
samir.k@optiscale.com

Folks — forwarding Samir's asks. Key negotiation points: 95th-percentile examples, cap overage exposure to 150% of committed tier in single month, map query credits to editor seats, onboarding credit tied to instrumentation milestones, show 12-month NPV with 6-month uplift and taper.

My recommended path: offer a structured concession rather than headline discount — i.e., +25% credit pool for first 6 months (applied to retention billing) then step down to +10% months 7–12. This preserves ARR while giving procurement the smoothing they want. Also offer a soft cap protection: if month >150% committed tier, bill spike at 125% rate for that month (we still capture overage revenue, but they get predictability).

Ben — can you run the math on NPV for the concession path vs. a straight 15% off for 12 months? Jordan — can you draft a short clause for the SOW that defines the onboarding milestone (instrumentation >= 80% endpoints instrumented + two-week run of data) and the credit release trigger? Karthik, any technical constraints on mapping query credits to editor seats for advanced dashboards?

Quotes included below (Samir's email).

Thanks,
Naomi

Samir — thanks for the clear asks. We reviewed internally and are prepared to move forward with a commercial that addresses procurement's concerns while keeping the economics intact. Summary below; revised attachments attached.

1) 95th-percentile example: see 'retention-tier-breakdown.pdf' — uses OptiScale sample traffic and shows credit application at 95th retention. In month-level examples, the nonlinear tiers smooth the peak charges so that the incremental cost between 50TB and 120TB is ~30% lower than a linear per-GB model.

2) Dashboard/query credits: we will map query credits to editor seats. Proposed mapping: each editor seat includes 200 query credits/day; additional credits purchased in 50k increments. Unlimited viewers remain complementary under your enterprise plan.

3) Concession / step-down: we will grant a temporary credit uplift: +25% credit pool for months 1–6, +10% for months 7–12. Billing will still report gross usage; credits applied at invoice calculation. Per your cap ask, we will cap exposure at 150% of committed tier. If a single-month usage exceeds 150% of tier, the overage will be invoiced but at a moderated multiplier (1.25x standard overage rate) for that month only.

4) Onboarding credit: we will provide a one-time $15k onboarding credit once OptiScale achieves instrumentation >=80% and a two-week stable run of data (definition included in SOW).

5) NPV / step-down math: Ben attached a short NPV worksheet that compares the concession path to a straight 15% discount. The concession path retains higher ARR after month 12 while giving meaningful near-term relief. See obs-pricing-matrix-v2.xlsx.

If this aligns, I'll send an updated SOW + redlined commercial terms and the DocuSign link for signatures. We are open to a procurement call tomorrow to walk through the cap language and the instrumentation acceptance criteria.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
